characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective, lodges at Baker Street with Watson.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.note: Narrator and Holmes's companion at Baker Street.

characters.name: Alexander Holder
characters.note: Senior partner of Holder & Stevenson, banking firm in Threadneedle Street; uncle of Mary and father of Arthur.

characters.name: Arthur Holder
characters.note: Son of Alexander Holder, accused of stealing the coronet gems.

characters.name: Mary Holder
characters.note: Niece of Alexander Holder, adopted daughter, who secretly aided Sir George Burnwell.

characters.name: Sir George Burnwell
characters.note: Gambler and villain, friend of Arthur, lover of Mary; the figure in the stable lane.

characters.name: Lucy Parr
characters.note: Second waiting-maid at Fairbank, who met her sweetheart at the back gate.

characters.name: Francis Prosper
aliases: the man with a wooden leg
characters.note: Greengrocer and sweetheart of Lucy Parr.

characters.name: the noble client
characters.note: Unnamed very high-ranking personage who deposited the Beryl Coronet as security; never named in the text.

characters.name: the police inspector
characters.note: Police officer who arrested Arthur and suggested Holder consult Holmes.

brief.place: Baker Street flat; City of London bank in Threadneedle Street; Fairbank, a square white stone house in Streatham with snowy lawn, iron gates, tradesmen's path and a stable lane behind.
brief.dress: Holder: sombre black frock-coat, shining hat, brown gaiters, pearl-grey trousers. Holmes in dressing-gown at home; disguised as a common loafer with worn coat, red cravat and seedy boots. Mary: dark, pale, dressed as a well-bred young woman. Arthur: shirt and trousers when caught at night, otherwise gentleman's dress. Sir George: well-dressed, handsome.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Bow-window at Baker Street; bank safe and morocco case; the Beryl Coronet of gold with thirty-nine beryls, one corner with three gems torn away; bureau with noiseless lock in the dressing-room; hall side window onto the stable lane; deep snow with footprints; a life-preserver and pistol.
depiction_rules: Show the coronet as a gold diadem with a visibly broken corner missing three gems.
Snow should be deep and white on the pavements and lawns, with a wintry sun.
Mary is pale with dark hair and eyes, and should appear grieved or flushed from weeping.
Keep Holmes in dressing-gown or disguise as the scene requires; avoid modern dress.
The noble client is never named and should be shown only obliquely or from behind.
